pr_title: nvs: hardening against bad sector close
pr_body:
A badly written sector close ate that has correct crc8 could allow
jumps outside the assigned flash area. This behavior is fixed.

Fixes #34382

Signed-off-by: Laczen JMS <laczenjms@gmail.com>

If sector is closed with this offset in closing ate, it mean that was treated as containing no valid data.

A sector is considered active or erased based on the data in last ate in a sector (the close ate). So the sector you have (which is not yet closed) would be considered as active. A restart would identify this sector as the active sector and when there is insufficient space close the sector -> empty closed sector. This would then no longer be considered a active sector. 

> GC from affected sector causes dead data resurrections.

Is this true ? If there is valid data it can be explainen by a write failure, if there only is dead data the only explanation I can see is a bad erase.

Before the flash sector was checked to avoid doing an erase of an already empty sector. This was useless as a already erased flash will not have a reduced life expectancy from an erase. So I just moved the compare after the erase to make sure that the erase has been succesfull.

issue_context.title: fs/nvs: if closing ATE has to high offset NVS iterates up to the end of flash.
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
If closing ate is valid (crc is ok) and close_ate.offset
has not allowed value GC will performed flash read above
NVS partition.


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/e3a25b3b3a141560d9d6c41121ab598e07a431c4

review_comments:
lack of check of case close_ate.offset > (fs->sector_size - ate_size)
need add service of close_ate.offset == (fs->sector_size - ate_size)
IMO not needed, see comment above.

lack of check of case `close_ate.offset > (fs->sector_size - ate_size)`
need add service of `close_ate.offset == (fs->sector_size - ate_size)`

I don't think we need to service this, IMO the simplest idea is to consider any ate as valid if `.offset< fs->sector_size - ate_size` . In that case the service of the special case is automatically done.
Almost, yes `.offset == (fs->sector_size - ate_size)` need special treatment
According to `.checkpatch.conf` you can have now 100 chars per line so ou do not have to break these `if`s
This probably will fit in one 100 character line.

Yes, but don't turn the rule around because then I would have to do lot's of changes :-) :-). I will leave this one as is and still try to keep the 80 char rule.

BTW, I think there is a 78 char rule on the PR description in github which already makes it very difficult to copy part of your code into the PR (e.g. as source for discussion).
